web.title: Impact of water-dispersible beadlets as a vehicle for the delivery of carotenoids to cultured cells
web.description:
Due to the lipophilic nature of carotenoids and their poor solubility in aqueous systems, in vitro investigations have previously been hampered by the lack of an appropriate bioavailable form. Studies using cell culture systems have made use of carotenoids solubilized in organic solvents such as ethanol, dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO), tetrahydrofuran (THF), and n-hexane. However several disadvantages are associated with these methods e.g. poor stability, toxicity, and crystallization of carotenoids in the culture medium.

Water-dispersible beadlets are one of the best delivery methods for carotenoids in vivo and have been used for in vivo studies for about two decades. Lycopene, β-carotene or other carotenoids delivered by beadlets were always absorbed in humans and animals and could be measured in plasma and tissues [2,3,9,15,16,21]. Nevertheless, there is little known about stability and cellular association of carotenoids in cell culture systems when delivered by beadlets.

The purities of crystalline lycopene, β-carotene, lutein and astaxanthin were 95, 95, 90, and 98%, respectively. All solvents used were HPLC grade. THF (99.9%) and hexane (99%) were further purified over an aluminum oxide column. Tissue culture vessels were obtained from VWR Scientific Products (San Diego, CA). Water-dispersible carotenoid beadlets (e.g. lycopene, β-carotene, lutein and astaxanthin) were kindly provided by BASF Aktiengesellschaft (Ludwigshafen, Germany).

Beadlets Carotenoid beadlets contained 10% (wt/wt) carotenoid in a matrix of fish-gelatine and glucose syrup, and an overall amount of approx. ∼5% of the antioxidants α-tocopherol, sodium ascorbate and ascorbylpalmitate. Beadlets without carotenoids were used as vehicles. A known quantity of the carotenoid beadlets was dissolved in 10 ml of phosphate buffered saline (PBS) and placed in a bath sonicator for five minutes to achieve a carotenoid concentration of 100 µM.

alginate, cellulose derivatives; Cyclodextrin Definitions the present invention relates to solid preparations of p-carotene in the form of beadlets which contain a high amount of p-carotene. P-Carotene is an organic, strongly colored red-orange pigment. Dietary p-carotene is a provitamin A compound, converting in the body to retinol (vitamin A). p-Carotene is frequently used as a vitamin A source in vitamin supplements and for coloring food. B-Carotene is insoluble in water and its solubility in fats and oils is found to be only low, as well.

Beadlets are a special form of powder preparations. They have typically a core which contains an active, e. g. B-carotene and matrix materials and optionally a covering or coating, which reduces the sticking of the particles. Beadlets are usually obtained by providing a dispersion of the respective active, here B-carotene, in water and/or a volatile organic solvent, grinding it to the desired particle size if necessary and then spray-drying suspension together with the matrix material.
